note: An early Latin apologist (c. AD 200) argues from the order of nature to one Ruler — the classic monotheistic argument, aimed at pagan polytheism. New author for the corpus. Filed under Trinity via the 'monotheism' tag, matching the existing Tertullian Apology 17 precedent (both are pagan-facing 'one God' arguments). Dating hinges on the Minucius-vs-Tertullian priority debate; 'c. 200' is the standard compromise. Verified verbatim against source_url (apologia-citations, web, 2026-08-24; Wallis, ANF vol. 4).
text: The bees have one king; the flocks one leader; among the herds there is one ruler. Can you believe that in heaven there is a division of the supreme power, and that the whole authority of that true and divine empire is sundered, when it is manifest that God, the Parent of all, has neither beginning nor end—that He who gives birth to all gives perpetuity to Himself—that He who was before the world, was Himself to Himself instead of the world?
